newsitem.title: FRANCE: Junior French government party seeks more tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Junior French government party seeks more tax cuts.

text.p: The leader of France's UDF party, the junior partner in the governing coalition, said on Monday he would push for cuts in value added tax (VAT) and a rethink of petrol duty increases in the 1997 budget when it is discussed in the National Assembly this week.
UDF leader Francois Leotard said the party would back the 1997 budget and that his call for VAT cuts and a petrol duty rethink was to improve the budget, not undermine it.
Leotard said in an interview in the daily Les Echos that the UDF would meet on Tuesday to see how a three-billion-franc loss in receipts could be filled if petrol duty rises were dropped.
"These two amendments are political signals," said Leotard, who comes from the same party as finance minister Jean Arthuis.

"By calling on the government to progressively reduce VAT and asking it to drop the plan to raise petrol duties, we wanted to highlight the need for other tax measures than a reduction in income tax," Leotard was quoted as saying.
"Our aims are not unrealistic. The gradual VAT reduction we are seeking would have no impact on the 1997 budget since it would only start from December (1997)," Leotard said.
"It would actually underline the government's intention that the extra (VAT) burden imposed in 1995 was not to be permanent."
